## Purpose and Scope

This RAD provides illustrative patterns and logical design guidance for securing the infrastructure-as-code pipeline — the mechanism through which all cloud infrastructure is provisioned, modified, and governed at Gainwell. Securing the IaC pipeline is foundational: a compromised or ungoverned IaC pipeline is equivalent to ungoverned console access to every AWS account.

**Governing ABBs**:
- [GUID-SEC-CLOUD-CLOUD-IAM-2.6.06 — Cloud Identity and Access Management](../GUID-SEC-CLOUD-CLOUD-IAM-2.6.06.md)
- [GUID-SEC-CLOUD-CSPM-2.6.03 — Cloud Security Posture Management](../GUID-SEC-CLOUD-CSPM-2.6.03.md) (IaC policy enforcement)
page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-IAC-RAD-3.6.03.md#rad-scope]

### RAD Scope

- Terraform pipeline security: OIDC-based pipeline authentication, state file security, plan approval gates
- Policy-as-code gates: static analysis of Terraform plans before apply
- IAM role generation patterns: permission boundary enforcement for programmatically created roles
- Secret management in IaC: prohibited patterns and approved injection patterns
- Drift detection: detecting manual console changes that diverge from IaC state

**IaC Platform Reference**: The enterprise IaC platform uses Terraform formations (reusable modules) and Terragrunt deployments (environment-specific configuration). See `iac/` in this repository for formations and deployment patterns.

## IaC Pipeline Security Architecture

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph Developer["Developer Workflow"]
        Dev["Developer\nLocal Terraform plan\n(terraform plan)"]
        PR["Pull Request\nCode review required\nSecurity scan triggered"]
    end

    subgraph Pipeline["CI/CD Pipeline (GitHub Actions)"]
        Lint["Lint Stage\nterraform fmt\nterraform validate"]
        SecurityScan["Security Scan\nCheckov / tfsec\nPolicy-as-code rules\nSecret detection"]
        Plan["Plan Stage\nterraform plan\nOIDC auth to AWS\n(no long-lived keys)"]
        PlanApproval["Plan Approval\nRequired for:\n- IAM changes\n- PHI account changes\n- SCP changes"]
        Apply["Apply Stage\nterraform apply\nChanges applied\nCloudTrail recorded"]
    end

    subgraph AWS["AWS — Target Accounts"]
        OIDC["OIDC Identity Provider\ngithub.com token\nRole assumption (no key)"]
        PipelineRole["Pipeline IAM Role\nLeast-privilege for\nprovisioning only\nPermission boundary applied"]
        StateBackend["Terraform State\nS3 + DynamoDB lock\nEncrypted (CMK)\nVersioned + access logged"]
    end

    Dev --> PR --> Lint --> SecurityScan --> Plan
    Plan --> PlanApproval --> Apply
    Plan -->|OIDC token| OIDC --> PipelineRole
    PipelineRole -->|read/write| StateBackend
```

[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-IAC-RAD-3.6.03.md#no-long-lived-pipeline-credentials]

### No Long-Lived Pipeline Credentials

The IaC pipeline **SHALL NOT** use IAM access keys (long-lived static credentials) for AWS authentication. GitHub Actions **SHALL** use OIDC federation to assume an IAM role:

```yaml
# GitHub Actions workflow step
- name: Configure AWS Credentials
  uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v4
  with:
    role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::{account}:role/github-terraform-pipeline-role
    aws-region: us-east-1
    # No access-key-id or secret-access-key — OIDC only
```
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-IAC-RAD-3.6.03.md#static-analysis-tools]

### Static Analysis Tools

The following checks **SHALL** run on every `terraform plan` output before apply approval:

| Check Category | Tool | Failure Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Security misconfigurations | Checkov | Block pipeline on HIGH/CRITICAL findings |
| IaC best practices | tfsec | Block on HIGH findings |
| Hardcoded secrets in IaC | detect-secrets / trufflehog | Block on any finding |
| Terraform format | terraform fmt | Block if formatting violations present |
| Cost estimation | Infracost | Advisory; does not block |
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-IAC-RAD-3.6.03.md#critical-policy-rules-block-on-violation]

### Critical Policy Rules (Block on Violation)

| Rule | Description |
|---|---|
| No public S3 buckets | `aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block` must be configured with all `true` |
| Encryption required | RDS, S3, EBS, DynamoDB resources must have encryption enabled |
| No wildcard IAM policies | IAM policies must not contain `Action: "*"` or `Resource: "*"` |
| No IAM user creation | `aws_iam_user` resources are prohibited (roles only) |
| CloudTrail must be enabled | Deletion of CloudTrail resources is prohibited |
| VPC flow logs required | VPC resources must have associated flow log configuration |
| KMS key rotation | KMS key resources must have `enable_key_rotation = true` |

[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-IAC-RAD-3.6.03.md#permission-boundary-enforcement]

### Permission Boundary Enforcement

All IAM roles created by Terraform **SHALL** have a permission boundary attached. The enterprise permission boundary policy limits the maximum effective permissions to a defined safe set:

```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "workload_role" {
  name                 = "${var.environment}-${var.service}-${var.component}-role"
  assume_role_policy   = data.aws_iam_policy_document.assume_policy.json
  permissions_boundary = "arn:aws:iam::${data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id}:policy/enterprise-workload-boundary"
  
  tags = {
    Environment     = var.environment
    Service         = var.service
    DataClass       = var.data_classification
    ManagedBy       = "terraform"
  }
}
```

**Required tags on all IAM roles**: `Environment`, `Service`, `ManagedBy: terraform`. Roles without `ManagedBy: terraform` tag **SHALL** generate a Config rule finding for unmanaged IAM resources.

[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-IAC-RAD-3.6.03.md#state-backend-requirements]

### State Backend Requirements

| Control | Configuration |
|---|---|
| State storage | S3 bucket in dedicated state account; not in workload account |
| Encryption | SSE-KMS with a dedicated state CMK |
| Versioning | S3 versioning enabled (state recovery capability) |
| Access logging | S3 access logging enabled |
| State locking | DynamoDB table for lock management |
| Bucket policy | Deny access to all principals except pipeline roles and state admins |

[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-IAC-RAD-3.6.03.md#state-file-sensitivity]

### State File Sensitivity

Terraform state files contain plaintext values of all resource attributes, including sensitive outputs. State **SHALL NOT** be stored in:
- Source code repositories
- Unencrypted S3 buckets
- Local developer workstations for production environments

[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-IAC-RAD-3.6.03.md#detecting-manual-console-changes]

### Detecting Manual Console Changes

All manual console changes to infrastructure resources are drift from the IaC state. Detection mechanisms:

- **AWS Config**: detects when resource configuration changes outside of CloudFormation/Terraform by comparing current state to recorded state
- **CloudTrail**: all API calls are logged; manual console changes appear as API calls from IAM user or assumed-role sessions that are not the pipeline role
- **Terraform plan drift detection**: scheduled `terraform plan` runs in a read-only mode that detect drift by identifying resources whose actual state differs from the Terraform state file

Detected drift in PHI accounts **SHALL** generate a High Security Hub finding and notify the security architecture team within 24 hours.
